requirement:
Habeas MUST locate its per-user configuration at
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/habeas/config.toml` on Unix when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is an absolute,
nonempty path, otherwise at `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`. On Windows it MUST
use `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`. `HOME` and `APPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. If no usable base directory can be
determined, an operation requiring user configuration MUST fail with an
explanatory diagnostic naming the variable.

The same user configuration MUST be usable across projects. Its location MUST
NOT be selected relative to the current project or changed by project settings.
User-local preferences for a project MAY remain in the user configuration;
workspace settings MUST use `habeas.toml` under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`.
rationale:
The marked tests cover each obligation in `requirements.configuration.user_location`.

**Unix XDG and HOME paths** (`tests/configuration.rs#fn[locations_use_absolute_xdg_values_and_platform_fallbacks]`)
- An absolute `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` gives `<xdg>/habeas/config.toml`.
- An empty or relative `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` with an absolute `HOME` falls back to `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`.
- A `HOME`-only lookup gives the same fallback.
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[base_directories_must_be_absolute_and_nonempty]` repeats the relative-XDG fallback with a literal absolute `HOME`.

**Windows path** (`tests/configuration.rs#fn[locations_use_absolute_xdg_values_and_platform_fallbacks]`)
- `APPDATA` gives `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`.

**Absolute and nonempty `HOME` and `APPDATA`** (`tests/configuration.rs#fn[base_directories_must_be_absolute_and_nonempty]`)
- An empty or relative `HOME` on Unix makes `user_config_path_from` fail.
- An empty or relative `APPDATA` on Windows makes it fail.
- Each error message must contain the variable name.

**No usable base directory** (`tests/configuration.rs#fn[locations_use_absolute_xdg_values_and_platform_fallbacks]`)
- With no variables set, Unix fails with an error naming `HOME`.
- With no variables set, Windows fails with an error naming `APPDATA`.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[authoring_uses_the_same_user_config_path_in_different_projects]` checks the same behavior end to end. `author` fails with a diagnostic naming `HOME` (or `APPDATA` on Windows) when the environment variables are removed.

**Same configuration across projects, not selected by project or changed by project settings** (`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[authoring_uses_the_same_user_config_path_in_different_projects]`)
- Two project fixtures are run, and the second has its own `habeas.toml`.
- Both runs fail on the one invalid user config at `first.config/habeas/config.toml`.
- The test asserts that the diagnostic names that path. A location chosen relative to the project or changed by project settings would not produce it.

`MAY` keeping user-local preferences in the user configuration imposes nothing to check. The `habeas.toml` workspace obligation is only a `{cite}` of `requirements.configuration.workspace_location` and is tested there. I found no gaps and no marking gaps.

Habeas MUST locate its per-user configuration at
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/habeas/config.toml` on Unix when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is an absolute,
nonempty path, otherwise at `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`. On Windows it MUST
use `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`. `HOME` and `APPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. If no usable base directory can be
determined, an operation requiring user configuration MUST fail with an
explanatory diagnostic naming the variable.
The same user configuration MUST be usable across projects. Its location MUST
NOT be selected relative to the current project or changed by project settings.
User-local preferences for a project MAY remain in the user configuration;
workspace settings MUST use `habeas.toml` under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`.
:::{req} workspace_location
Habeas MUST search from its invocation directory upward for the nearest enclosing
`habeas.toml`. It MUST use that file alone, without merging ancestor workspace
files. A library operation given a project root MUST search from that root unless
its current directory is inside the project, in which case it MUST start there.
The directory containing the selected file defines the base for its relative
paths; it does not replace the Cargo and mdBook project root. A missing file MUST
mean absent workspace settings. Discovery MUST report unreadable candidate files
rather than silently selecting an ancestor. Loading MUST NOT create the file.
